title: Dune-inspired tactical prototype in Godot 4
author: Due_Arachnid2975
selftext:
Hello!

I'm putting together a Dune-themed 2D single player game, inspired by Syndicate, one of my all time favourites.

Right now it's in the very preliminary stage, I'm just working out some of the mechanics, there is no artwork at all (I'm gonna prototype it this way and if/when I see if the mechanics are fun to play I'm planning on involving some artists for the graphics) and the current mechanics are showcased via a tutorial level + a placeholder mission. 

The gameplay is absolutely not balanced yet and that's why I'm posting it here to gather some early reactions and comments.

Some of the current features are:

**Stealth.** Commandos-style vision cones drawn on the ground, a cone that stops at a rock means he genuinely can't see past it. Detection fills gradually; stance, distance, movement and angle all feed the rate.

**Holtzman shields.** Bullets and fast blades bounce off. Only a *slow* blade gets through. Shield energy can never reach zero, so you have to change how you attack.

**Squad command.** Two Fremen, ordered around in a time-slowed command mode. Orders are refused beyond a certain command link range to favor tactical thinking, so you can't micromanage a scout you've sent over the hill.

**Prescience.**  A brief slow-motion read of what enemies are *committed* to doing. One likely near future, not branching timelines, and it walks real AI intent rather than faking it.

**Sandworms.** Movement on open sand makes vibration. Crouch < walk < sprint, gunfire spikes it. Rock is silent and rock is safe. Enough vibration and a worm commits to whatever's making the most of it.

I strongly recommend to play the tutorial mission first in order to learn all the mechanics

There's a full mission tying it together: cripple a spice harvester and escape before the worm arrives. The comms beacon is skippable (halves the reinforcement response), and the worm arrival isn't a cutscene: the worm system reacts to a crippled crawler being the loudest thing in the desert.

You can clone the repo here and run it as a Godot project [https://github.com/teidenzero/Dune](https://github.com/teidenzero/Dune)
